DeCosemo was named the seventh head women’s soccer coach at Central Michigan University by Zyzelewski Family Vice President/Director of Athletics Amy Folan on December 10, 2025.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nDeCosemo brought an extensive background in collegiate coaching across multiple levels, all in the state of Michigan, upon arrival in Mount Pleasant.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nThe Stokesley, England-native logged three dominant years at the helm for NAIA Aquinas College, where he posted a 55-5-7 overall record, an undefeated 31-0-3 record in the Wolverine Hoosier Athletic Conference, and five total WHAC Championships—three regular season, two tournament.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nDeCosemo’s leadership at Aquinas led to the program’s best finish in the NAIA national tournament as the Saints reached the national quarterfinals in both 2022 and 2023. Aquinas defeated eight nationally ranked teams during his tenure, four times doing so in the NAIA tournament.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nThe Saints racked up 10 NAIA All-America nods as well as 25 all-conference selections, 19 of which were first team. Aquinas appeared in the NAIA national rankings wire-to-wire in his tenure and was a top-10 mainstay for the 2023 and 2024 campaigns.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nDirectly prior to CMU, DeCosemo was an assistant coach at Western Michigan, which swept the Mid-American Conference regular season and tournament titles in his lone season in Kalamazoo in 2025. He has also been an assistant coach for the Aquinas men (2019-21) and NCAA II Saginaw Valley State women (2017-18).\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nAs a player, DeCosemo was a three-time Great Lakes Intercollegiate Athletic Conference Champion at NCAA II Northwood University, where he earned all-conference and United Soccer Coaches All-Region honors and led the Timberwolves to the NCAA Midwest Regional Final (round of 16) in his 2015 senior season.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nHe graduated from Northwood in 2016 with a bachelor’s degree in business administration, focused in marketing, and a minor in management.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nDeCosemo competed for Lansing United in Lansing, Mich. from 2014-17, then again when the team was reprised from 2022-25 for eight total seasons of semi-professional competition in the Lansing area. In the meantime, he played for Grand Rapids FC in Grand Rapids, Mich.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nHe has also been the Director of Coaching for Nationals Capital Area Soccer club in Lansing since 2016.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nDeCosemo is joined by his wife, Allison, and their son, Oliver.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cstrong>THE DECOSEMO FILE\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr In her role with the SAAC, she represented the field hockey program to build community relations, organize athletic events, and serve as the voice of the program for the development of athletics.  \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMurray attended St. Gerard's School in Dublin, Ireland where she earned four letters in field hockey and played for the Muckross Hockey Club.
